answer_text:
# 📊 Grade to Percentage Calculator

Here's everything you need to convert grades to percentages — including formulas, a reference table, and examples!

---

## 🔢 Basic Formula

To find the percentage, divide the mark by the maximum possible mark, then multiply by 100.

> **Formula:**
> ## `Percentage = (Scored Marks ÷ Total Marks) × 100`

---

## 📐 Examples

### ✅ Single Test/Exam
If a student scored **85** on an exam with a maximum mark of **100**:
> 85 ÷ 100 = 0.85 × 100 = **85%**

### ✅ Multiple Tests
If a student scored **92** on the first exam and **88** on the second, with a total maximum of **200**:
> (92 + 88) ÷ 200 × 100 = 180 ÷ 200 × 100 = **90%**

### ✅ Weighted Grades
For example: 67% for an essay worth 15%, 75% for a midterm worth 35%, and 72% for a final worth 50%:
> 67% × 0.15 + 75% × 0.35 + 72% × 0.50 = **72.3% ≈ C-**

---

## 🔠 Letter Grade to Percentage Chart (US Standard)

| Letter Grade | Percentage Range | GPA |
|---|---|---|
| A+ | 97–100% | 4.0 |
| A | 93–96% | 4.0 |
| A- | 90–92% | 3.7 |
| B+ | 87–89% | 3.3 |
| B | 83–86% | 3.0 |
| B- | 80–82% | 2.7 |
| C+ | 77–79% | 2.3 |
| C | 73–76% | 2.0 |
| C- | 70–72% | 1.7 |
| D+ | 67–69% | 1.3 |
| D | 63–66% | 1.0 |
| D- | 60–62% | 0.7 |
| F | Below 60% | 0.0 |

This is the standard grading system for US schools and universities. However, grading may vary among schools, classes, and teachers — always check beforehand which system is used in your case.

---

## 🧮 Quick Reference Calculator

| Score (out of 20) | Percentage | Grade |
|---|---|---|
| 20/20 | 100% | A+ |
| 18/20 | 90% | A- |
| 16/20 | 80% | B- |
| 14/20 | 70% | C- |
| 12/20 | 60% | D- |
| Below 12/20 | Below 60% | F |

For instance, if you score 18/20, divide the correct answers (18) by the total questions (20) and multiply by 100 → **(18 ÷ 20) × 100 = 90%**

---

## 🎓 Final Grade Formula

Your **final grade** can be calculated using:
> **Grade = Exam Worth × Exam Score + (1 – Exam Worth) × Current Grade**

---

> 💡 **Tip:** Grade ranges may vary by school, so always check your syllabus for the exact grading scale your teacher uses.
